title: Eastern Michigan University students launch first student-led hackathon after Google I/O experience
text:
Eastern Michigan University students launch first student-led hackathon after Google I/O experience
A. S. Brooks
Eastern Michigan University students Chanuth Jayatissa and Karthikeya Thota attended the invitation-only Google I/O 2026 developer conference, after founding the university’s first Google Developer Group and achieving success in national hackathons, according to a Jul. 22 announcement.
Jayatissa, an international student from Sri Lanka, joined forces with Thota to compete in hackathons and eventually recognized an opportunity to bring together fellow computer science students at EMU. "Initially, when we did Hackathons, we didn't win, of course. But we just kept going because the experience of meeting new people who are just so driven to build and create in computer science was really fascinating," Jayatissa said. He added that discovering the concept of a Google Developer Group inspired them: "I found out through attending Hackathons that there was this thing called 'Google Developer Group.' I was telling Karthikeya, 'We have to start this; this is going to be a great opportunity.' Then in the following fall, we started our GDG here on campus."
Since launching EMU's first Google Developer Group in 2025, Jayatissa and Thota have fostered a collaborative community focused on exploring technology and competing nationwide. Their leadership led them not only to Google I/O but also to the Google Developer Group Summit for student leaders worldwide. "I believe they selected our group because we share our story on [GDG] platforms," Jayatissa said. "At that point, we had won the best club and best new student organization on campus, won multiple Hackathons, including the largest one in the Midwest, all while promoting Google technologies." At these events they learned strategies for organizational growth: "It gave us advice on how to manage the group when we got back home... We learned so much and were able to bring back so much knowledge to run the club ten times better than we did before." The trip was supported by both Google—covering travel expenses—and Honors Travel Grants from EMU's Honors College.
Looking ahead, Jayatissa and Thota are organizing "Hack the Nest," EMU’s first student-led hackathon scheduled for November 14-15. The event aims to unite hundreds of students with industry professionals while establishing EMU as a regional innovation hub.
Eastern Michigan University prepares students for significant societal contributions through its educational focus; it offers more than 200 undergraduate majors and minors as well as graduate programs; its campus features historic architecture alongside modern facilities supporting student success; it has gained national recognition for various programs; James Smith served as president, all according to the official website.
